summary.intent: Rebase a feature branch (escalator/accessibility scoring work) off main to pick up a fix for elevation issues.
summary.outcome: Discovered main had not moved and the real fix lived in unmerged PR #8 (elevation-cache-only branch); rebased onto that branch instead, rewired scoring to use cached step measurements, integrated into main.ts, updated/added tests (13 passing), and verified in-browser that two example stairways now score distinctly with no API calls.

repo: measurements.ts on elevation-cache-only provides real per-stairway step counts from a cached repo file instead of an async elevation API call
Scoring now sources step counts from the cache for 859 of 1,123 stairways, falling back to rating-based estimates for only 264 (down from 1,076)
Playwright's Node runtime requires an explicit `with { type: 'json' }` import attribute to import the metrics JSON module (needed in measurements.ts)
A 1-star-rated stairway can legitimately be a scoring candidate once real step counts are used, which changed empty-state test assumptions

code.finding: Added `with { type: 'json' }` import attribute to the metrics JSON import so Playwright/Node's resolver can load it; flagged as a possible conflict point with PR #8

Existing test file was missing `readFileSync` import; added it. Also appended new tests including one pinning Aurelious Walker vs Quesada Gardens scores to prevent them collapsing to the same value again
Integrated the escalator assessment into the rebased main.ts at the anchors used by the elevation-cache-only branch

workflow: When asked to 'rebase off main' but main hasn't moved, check open PRs for branches that actually contain the intended fix rather than assuming main is up to date
When repeated rebase conflicts hit the same files across multiple commits, it's cleaner to reset onto the target branch and re-apply/rebuild changes than to keep resolving conflicts commit-by-commit
Keep a backup branch (e.g. backup-escalator-retrofit) before destructive rebase/reset operations to preserve original history
Node's bare-specifier module resolution differs from Vite's; use esbuild to bundle scratch/ad-hoc verification scripts when Vite isn't available
Verify rebased/integrated changes both via full test suite and manually in the browser (dev server) before committing

friction: Initial instruction to 'rebase off main' was based on a false premise — main hadn't changed, so a literal rebase would be a no-op
Four rounds of merge conflicts in the same two files during initial rebase attempt onto elevation-cache-only, requiring a reset-and-rebuild approach instead
Node couldn't resolve a bare specifier for a JSON import the way Vite does, requiring a workaround via esbuild bundling and later an import attribute fix
Playwright test failures required two follow-up fixes: missing `with { type: 'json' }` attribute and a missing `readFileSync` import
An empty-state test assertion broke because a 1-star stairway could now be a valid candidate, requiring test logic update
open_items: Work is now coupled to unmerged PR #8 (elevation-cache-only) and should land after that PR merges
The added `with { type: 'json' }` import attribute in measurements.ts should be flagged/checked for conflicts with PR #8's own version of the file
Old commit history preserved on `backup-escalator-retrofit` branch — not yet cleaned up/deleted
